title: Staged Zero-Trust Upgrade Guide for Private Inference
body:
Purpose:
This doc proposes a staged, zero-trust-first approach for upgrading private deployments (VPC/on-prem) across control plane, runtime, and operator agent components. The goal is to minimize blast radius, preserve API compatibility for customer endpoints, and provide strong auth + key lifecycle guarantees during and after migration.

Scope:
- Private deployments (VPC, on-prem appliance, air-gapped variants) that run Redwood’s control plane agent + serving runtime
- Upgrade touches: control plane binaries, runtime (inference engine), agent auth flow, certs/KMS integration, TF modules that manage network & IAM glue
- Not covered: customer application stack, dedicated-hosted regional endpoints (hosted API is separate)

High-level approach (staged):
1) Preparation and assessment (canary lab)
   - Inventory nodes by role: control-plane (k8s/api-proxy), runtime pools (GPU types), edge proxies, management agents. Produce a CSV with: hostname/instance-id, runtime-version, kernel/driver versions, cert-version, IRL (restart window).
   - Telemetry baseline: capture 72h of tail-latency, token-throughput, error-rate broken down by model and sequence-length buckets. Save as artifact (s3://redwood-playbooks/zt-upgrade/).
   - Define SLIs and rollback thresholds: 5xx > 0.5% sustained for 5m, p95 latency increase > 30% sustained for 10m, token-cost regression > 12% on synthetic prompt set.

2) Zero-trust bake (pre-upgrade, non-disruptive)
   - Introduce agent mTLS and mutual auth in a shadow mode: new control plane accepts both current bearer-token agents and mTLS-auth agents. Agents configured to present certs but also keep old token fallback until cutover window.
   - KMS integration: configure read-only access to KMS for cert retrieval on canary nodes. Do NOT rotate customer KMS keys during this phase.
   - Terraform note: add optional module variable enable_mtls_shadow = true to private-deployments network module. Provide tf-shim that creates cert-issuing service account and narrow IAM binding. Document in TF module notes (see appendix TF snippets).

3) Control plane & API compatibility tiering
   - Introduce a compatibility shim layer: the control plane accepts v1/v1-beta API calls and routes them to the upgraded control-plane component if the call surface matches the backwards compatibility table. For incompatible calls, respond with a 426 upgrade-required + machine-readable hint (recommended client upgrade).
   - Compatibility table: method, request schema delta, suggested transformation, fallback behavior. Keep this table as a living CSV.
   - Rollout: start with canary control plane behind a traffic mirror and replay traffic to the canary for 48h. Capture diffs.

4) Runtime upgrade strategy (non-disruptive concurrency)
   - Build runtime images with two variants: new-runtime and compatibility-mode-new-runtime (runtime runs new code but honors legacy KV and API shims).
   - Node labeling: use rollout labels (zt-upgrade-phase=canary|stage|stable). Use small batch drains: 1–3 nodes per pool per 10m depending on pool size and capacity cushion.
   - Warm KV/caches: before directing live traffic, pre-warm KV caches using the same request sampling used in the telemetry baseline step.

5) Certificate & key rotation plan
   - Staged cert roll: issue interim certs valid for 90 days from internal CA; deploy to agent shadow mode. After successful canary, rotate for stage nodes, then GA.
   - HSM/KMS: create an audit log of KMS Get/Decrypt calls during rotation. If audit anomalies present, pause and investigate.

6) Rollback and automatic fallback policies
   - Multi-layer fallback:
     a) Runtime level: if node p95 latency or 5xx exceeds threshold, mark node unready and shift requests to remaining pool.
     b) Control plane policy: automatic failover to previous control plane replica set for matching client IDs when compatibility mismatch or SLO violation detected.
     c) API gateway: return synthetic 503 with explanatory header when broader regional fallback is invoked.
   - Safe rollback checklist: pre-staged snapshot of runtime config, tf state backup, export of control-plane DB snapshot (logical), agent-token-cache dump (redact secrets), and telemetry trace ids for the impacted window.

7) Observability & verification
   - Traces: add a custom tag upgrade.phase with values: prep, shadow-mtls, canary-control, canary-runtime, stage, stable, rollback. All requests touching upgraded code paths must surface this tag.
   - Evals: run the standard eval-suite (production prompt set) against canary runtimes every 30m. Compare output quality metrics (BLEU-style and human-sample spot checks).
   - Cost instrumentation: measure token-per-request delta and infer unit-cost; if > 10% deviation for 3 consecutive eval runs, trigger alert and pause.

8) Terraform and infra module notes (practical):
   - New module variables: enable_shadow_mtls (bool), mtls_ca_secret_name (string), agent_service_account (string), cert_rotation_window_days (int).
   - Keep the existing public TF outputs stable; do NOT remove old outputs until 2 release cycles after GA to avoid breaking customers consuming outputs.
   - Migration pattern: introduce 'tf shim' resources behind feature flags. Example pattern: resource "aws_iam_role" "mtls_issuer" { count = var.enable_shadow_mtls ? 1 : 0 } — callers can flip flag gradually.
   - State migration: never rename tf resources in place. If refactor is required, use a new resource + state mv plan and record it in PR. Include a migration-runbook snippet that operators can run to move state.

9) Runbook (operator checklist) - concise actionable steps for a single canary wave:
   - Step 0: validate canary lab (baseline metrics present)
   - Step 1: enable enable_shadow_mtls=true in tf on canary namespace, apply, wait for agent certs to appear
   - Step 2: deploy control-plane canary behind mirror, enable tracing with upgrade.phase=canary-control
   - Step 3: watch eval results & telemetry for 2h, check SLOs, human spot-check 10 outputs
   - Step 4: drain 1 runtime node, replace with new-runtime image (compat-mode), pre-warm caches
   - Step 5: after 30m of stable metrics, proceed to next batch; if thresholds breached, run rollback script: scripts/rollback-to-prev.sh <wave-id>

10) Safety checks and gating
   - Must-have checks before any stage migration: terraform plan has zero destroys on shared resources, smoke test (health-check endpoint /health returns expected payload), control-plane DB replication lag < 5s, GPU drivers within supported range.
   - Emergency abort: support runbook must include an abort token (short-lived JWT) that temporarily disables the canary control plane from accepting production traffic. This token issuance requires 2-approver flow (SRE + Eng lead).

11) Open questions / decisions to make
   - Can we avoid any agent-token rotation for customers who cannot accept downtime? If not, define minimal token TTL and an overlap plan.
   - For air-gapped installs, what's the manual CA issuance workflow? We need a crisp sub-doc for that.
   - Should TF modules expose a managed KMS key or leave KMS ownership entirely to the customer? Security prefs differ by regulated customers.

Appendix A — TF snippet (example):
# tf example (pseudo)
# feature-flagged mtls issuer role
variable "enable_shadow_mtls" { type = bool default = false }
resource "aws_iam_role" "mtls_issuer" {
  count = var.enable_shadow_mtls ? 1 : 0
  name = "redwood-mtls-issuer-${var.env}"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.mtls_assume.json
}

Appendix B — Example rollback commands
- tf state pull > /tmp/tf-state-<wave>.json
- scripts/export-controlplane-db.sh > /tmp/cp-backup-<wave>.sql
- ./scripts/mark-wave-rollback.sh --wave <wave-id> --reason "p95-latency-regression"

Appendix C — Quick validation checklist (post-cutover)
- smoke: curl -sS https://private-api.internal/status | jq .version == "v2.1-zt"
- latency: p95_inference_last_30m < baseline_p95 * 1.2
- errors: 5xx_30m < 0.5%
- outputs: run eval-suite --target canary-runtime --compare baseline --report /tmp/zt-eval-<ts>.json

Notes to self (working items):
- Draft a short customer-facing FAQ explaining what zero-trust means for their tokens and certs (Priya to lead).
- Wire up a terraform validator in CI that detects renames and suggests state-mv patterns (Arjun task).
- Add a special alert channel #zt-upgrade-watch for the first 48h after GA.

End — this doc is intentionally prescriptive but lightweight. Next actions: convert key sections into a Confluence runbook page, create a linear ticket for air-gap CA workflow, and open the TF PR that adds enable_shadow_mtls flag behind feature toggle.
